results.summary: Instructions. An instruction is $\mathrm{inc}(j,x)$ (increment register $j$, go to state $x$), $\mathrm{dec}(j,x,y)$ (if register $j$ is positive, decrement it and go to $x$; otherwise go to $y$) or $\mathrm{halt}$. Registers are indexed by $\mathbb N$ and hold natural numbers; a register file is a map $\rho:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

results.title: Correctness of the precision program
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The precision program is total, and for every $c\in\mathbb N^5$ it accepts $c$ if and only if $\mathrm{decide}(c)=\mathrm{true}$, if and only if $\operatorname{accepts}(c)$. Its outcome on an input that fails an early test is $\mathbf{reject}$.

results.title: The precision machine halts exactly on acceptance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M_{\rm prec}=\mathrm{low}(S_{\rm prec})$, a primitive program valid for its register count $r_{\rm prec}$, with $5$ inputs. For every $c\in\mathbb N^5$: When $\operatorname{accepts}(c)$ fails, the run of $M_{\rm prec}$ never halts, although the ideal program is total.
